display.purpose: The dommy page's thesis; the figures band title runs close to it.

headline.purpose: Dommy page example headings that state the claim the example proves; the home Packages heading.

subtitle.purpose: Section headings in docs prose, the guide ending, the wordmark.

readout.purpose: Write-board figures and every posted number, tabular; read-out boxes, result plates and band figures scale from it.

label.purpose: Board labels, code captions, table heads, the keyboard hint; slate.

code.purpose: Code panes, inline code and the install line only.

motion.name: control-shift
motion.purpose: Primary and solid actions changing background, a package plate changing its border colour; only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: write-flash
motion.value: outline 3px solid (signal-ink | flag), offset 2px, to transparent over 700ms ease-out
motion.purpose: The write board outlines each element a small change touched (up to 100 records): signal ink for edits and moves, flag for inserted nodes. Under reduced motion the outline shows and hides without fading.

motion.name: scoreboard-slide
motion.purpose: A home scoreboard row sliding to its new place when a car passes another (a FLIP move, one tick every 1.5s). Under reduced motion the rows jump.

motion.name: flap-turn
motion.value: two drum letters 55ms apart, each a 100ms ease-out drop from perspective(40px) rotateX(-75deg); each tile 18ms after the one before it
motion.purpose: A changed split-flap letter turning through two drum letters and settling. Under reduced motion the letter changes in place.

motion.name: card-turn
motion.purpose: A memory card turning over in place (a 3D flip), and a found pair's face filling signal. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; otherwise the card changes side in place.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Demo and source stack; the opening bands go to one column.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Rail becomes chips or plates; tighter demo stage and board figures; smaller code.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Two-column demo list rows go to one column.

breakpoints.name: header-wrap
breakpoints.purpose: The site header wraps to two rows: wordmark and languages first, the sections second.

breakpoints.name: game-side
breakpoints.purpose: A game panel at least this wide sets its readouts, buttons and status in a column beside the board (up to 28rem); narrower, they sit in a bar above it.

breakpoints.name: game-tight
breakpoints.purpose: A game panel under this width sets its counters at 2.25rem instead of 2.75rem.

narrative.overview:
The whole site reads like a race timing screen: an asphalt ground, graphite ink and bands, white panels where the live demos run, signal yellow for whatever is current, leading or posted, and flag red for the one kind of write that matters most. Every number that the reader might compare (DOM writes, sizes, times, places) is set in a condensed display face with tabular figures, as a timing tower would post it. The world is carried by palette, type and plates, not by a story: headings say plainly what they show. The site is built with the library it documents, so the visual system is there to make each live demo and its write count legible, not to decorate around them.

Density is that of a working tool: a docs rail, a demo beside its source, a write board under each demo. The home page (`/`) opens on a graphite band, its copy set to the top beside the board: the headline of what reely is, a lead, three figures the build measured of every package, the button down to the packages, the credits naming which package draws which part of the board, and a live split-flap scoreboard on a white panel; below it, every package on the same white plate, in the order they stack. Every other package has a page at its name (`/signals`, `/queue`): the same graphite band with the package name, why it exists, its install line and links, beside its measured facts as a timing sheet, then one live example on asphalt with its source, and the names of the values it exports as code chips. The dommy page (`/dommy`) is the same world at a larger scale: a graphite band opens it with the thesis and the first live demo, plain example sections follow on asphalt, and a graphite band of measured figures closes it. A game (`/games/memory`) is a whole small app in the same world: a graphite band with the title, one line, one figure counted from its sources and the credits beside the game on its white panel with the write board under it, then the modules that run it, each a section on asphalt with its source. Nothing is lifted by shadow; depth is the step from asphalt to white panel to graphite band.

Motion answers the reader: the write board outlines the nodes a change touched and fades the outline, controls shift colour in 120ms, and a memory card turns over in 360ms. The one thing that moves on its own is the home page's scoreboard, a live race the reader can pause; it stops while off screen or in a hidden tab, and under reduced motion its rows jump and its letters change without turning.
keyCharacteristics: Asphalt ground, white demo panels, graphite bands and code panes; flat, bordered with 1px hairlines.
Signal yellow marks state (current page, leader, posted result, primary action), never fills a surface for decoration.
Big Shoulders Display at weight 800 for headings and every posted number; Atkinson Hyperlegible for prose; JetBrains Mono only for code. In Russian, their Cyrillic stand-ins (see Typography).
Small, even corners (3 to 6px); plates, not pills.
Every live demo ships with its write board; every code pane is the module that runs.

rules.name: The Signal Is State Rule
rules.body: Signal yellow means "this one": current, leading, posted, or the one primary action. A yellow surface that does not answer "which one?" does not belong.

rules.name: The Signal Ink Rule
rules.body: Yellow as text or a small mark on asphalt or white is signal ink; pure signal is for fills under graphite text and for anything on graphite.

rules.name: The Flag Means Nodes Rule
rules.body: Flag red marks node insertions and removals and nothing else: no error states, no emphasis, no hover. A failure is a white plate with a 2px graphite border; a moved node is graphite and signal ink, because it is no new node.

rules.name: The Posted Number Rule
rules.body: Any figure that changes or is compared (writes, sizes, times, places, step numbers) is set in the display face at 800 with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Mono Is Code Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only for code: code panes, inline code, code chips in demo results, and the install line. Labels and numbers never borrow it.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, labels and navigation are sentence case with default tracking; the build has no uppercase or letter-spaced labels.

rules.name: The Flat Screen Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift. To separate, change the tone (asphalt, panel, graphite) or draw a hairline; never add a shadow.

dos: Do put the write board under every live demo, and show the module that renders it in a code pane beside it.
Do set every posted figure in the display face at 800 (Big Shoulders Display; its Russian stand-in) with tabular figures.
Do mark the current item with a signal plate or underline, and draw focus as a 3px graphite ring on light surfaces and a 3px signal ring on graphite.
Do separate layers by tone and 1px hairlines (line on light, slate on graphite).
Do move only in answer to the reader, with the home page's scoreboard as the one live exception, and under reduced motion drop transitions, fades and turns.
donts: Don't use box-shadow or any lift; the screen is flat.
Don't set signal yellow as text on asphalt or white; use signal ink.
Don't use flag red for anything but nodes added or removed.
Don't use JetBrains Mono outside code, or a third accent hue.
Don't round past 6px or use pill shapes.
Don't add uppercase, letter-spaced labels or kickers above headings; a heading states its point on its own.
